expectations.text: A canonical model file exists separate from the generated JSON Schema
expectations.evidence: with_skill/outputs/datamodel/model.yaml is the canonical model; the JSON Schema is generated separately at datamodel/exports/draft/schema.json (response.md: 'Both schemas are now generated from that one file').

expectations.text: Position is modelled as a value type without its own identity (a datatype, or explicitly marked as an embedded value without a key)
expectations.evidence: model.yaml places Position under the top-level `datatypes:` section (not `classes:`), with attributes lat/lon/altitude and no identifier; response.md table: 'Position | value type'.

expectations.text: Pollutant is modelled as an extensible or externally governed code list, not a closed enum or an undocumented plain string
expectations.evidence: model.yaml `enumerations: Pollutant: extensible: true` with a `vocabulary:` block (uri http://dd.eionet.europa.eu/vocabulary/aq/pollutant, retrieved 2026-11-23, subset: true) and six coded values with URIs.

expectations.text: The station kind is modelled as a closed enumeration with traffic, industrial and background
expectations.evidence: model.yaml `StationKind: extensible: false` with values traffic, industrial, background; schema.json has enum [traffic, industrial, background]; generated XSD keeps xs:enumeration.

expectations.text: The meaning of the integer validity and verification codes is flagged as ambiguous
expectations.evidence: response.md item 4: '`validity` and `verification` are bare `xs:int` with no named code list. They look like the EEA AQD flags, but the XSD doesn't say so (A-004).'

expectations.text: The missing coordinate reference system for lat/lon is flagged
expectations.evidence: response.md item 7: 'Position has no coordinate reference system. Lat/lon have no stated CRS (I assumed WGS 84)'. model.yaml Position: 'CRS is not stated in S1; WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) decimal degrees assumed (A-005)'.

expectations.text: Identifier issues are flagged (xs:ID values only unique within one document, and/or overlap of id and stationCode)
expectations.evidence: response.md item 1: '`@id` is `xs:ID`: it is unique only within one document ... `stationCode` has no uniqueness rule.' Model: Station identifier {attribute: stationCode}; id described as 'Only unique within one delivery'.

expectations.text: The observation volume (roughly 21 million per year: 400 x 6 x 24 x 365) is recorded in the canonical model, not only in prose
expectations.evidence: model.yaml Observation `nfr: volume: 21000000/year`, `growth: "~57,600 per day (400 stations x 6 pollutants x 24 hours), ~21 M per year"`, plus accessPaths.

expectations.text: The high observation volume leads to an API design note (e.g. observations as a separate, paginated resource rather than nested in station documents)
expectations.evidence: response.md: 'That doesn't change the logical model, but the API should: page time series, with a query by sampling point (or station + pollutant) and time range; store observations partitioned by time; upsert on (samplingPoint, begin).' Model nfr notes: 'API must page time series'. Weaker than without_skill: it does not explicitly say to split observations out of nested station documents for reads.

expectations.text: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
expectations.evidence: Ran jsonschema Draft202012Validator.check_schema on exports/draft/schema.json: OK. Instance with observation value null: 0 errors (value is anyOf number/null).

expectations.text: The JSON Schema keeps the observation value required but nullable, matching the XSD where the element is mandatory but nillable
expectations.evidence: schema.json Observation required: [begin, end, value, validity, verification], value anyOf number/null. Tested: value=null valid; value key removed gives "'value' is a required property".

expectations.text: An XSD generated from the canonical model accepts the same documents as the original 2.1 XSD: a sample delivery valid against observations.xsd also validates against the generated XSD (checked with lxml)
expectations.evidence: lxml (python -I): examples/sample-delivery.xml validates against the original observations.xsd (True) and the generated exports/draft/schema.xsd (True); a self-written minimal doc (no altitude, nil value, validity 0, verification 7, offset-less dateTime, pollutant 'weird') is also valid in both. CAVEAT: the generated XSD adds lat/lon minInclusive/maxInclusive, so a doc with lat=95 passes the original but fails the generated XSD (verified). This is disclosed in response.md (D-002: 'a document with lat = 95 passed 2.1 but fails the generated XSD'). 'Accepts the same documents' is therefore not strictly true; passed on the specified sample-delivery check.

expectations.text: The pollutant code list is linked to a named standard vocabulary (e.g. the EEA/Eionet air quality pollutant vocabulary) with its register URI and a snapshot date or version, or reusing such a vocabulary is recommended to the user with the reason
expectations.evidence: model.yaml Pollutant `vocabulary: uri: http://dd.eionet.europa.eu/vocabulary/aq/pollutant, name: AQD - Air Quality Pollutants, publisher: European Environment Agency (Eionet Data Dictionary), version: null, retrieved: 2026-11-23`, with per-value URIs (4 marked unverified). Propagated as x-vocabulary in schema.json.

claims.claim: The generated XSD gives the same verdict as the original except for the lat/lon range
claims.evidence: Reproduced the sample and lat=95 cases with lxml.
model.yaml notes mark them 'not verified on the register'.

suggestions.assertion: An XSD generated from the canonical model accepts the same documents as the original 2.1 XSD: a sample delivery valid against observations.xsd also validates against the generated XSD (checked with lxml)
suggestions.reason: A single valid sample cannot detect tightenings. with_skill's generated XSD adds lat/lon range facets and rejects a lat=95 document the original accepts, yet still passes. Add edge-case documents (out-of-range lat, missing offset, unknown codes, nil altitude) or require that any tightening be explicitly disclosed.

suggestions.assertion: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
suggestions.reason: Both runs pass trivially, since a nullable value is the obvious mapping of nillable. Together with the 'required but nullable' assertion this is largely redundant.

No assertion checks whether the JSON Schema enforces assumed, unconfirmed code lists. without_skill enforces validity/verification enums in JSON (rejecting 2.1-valid data), while with_skill keeps them open. This meaningful design difference is not graded.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 4-7, 10 and 11 do not discriminate (both runs pass). The discriminating ones are Position as value type, pollutant code list, volume in the model, and vocabulary link.
